ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A square of area $125 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ was divided into five parts of equal area - four squares and one L-shaped figure as shown in the picture. Find the length of the shortest side of the L-shaped figure.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a large square; at the upper-right position inside, there is a 2×2 block composed of four identical small squares; this 2×2 block is against the top side and right side of the large square, and the remaining areas on the left side and lower side connect into an L shape. Reasoning: The area of the large square is 125 cm², so the side length is √125=5√5 cm. The five parts have equal areas, therefore the area of each part is 125÷5=25 cm². The area of each of the four squares is 25 cm², so the side length of each small square is 5 cm. The shortest side of the L shape in the figure is precisely the remaining width after subtracting the side lengths of two small squares from the side length of the large square, namely 5√5−2·5=5√5−10=5(√5−2) cm.

raw_record.question_text: A square of area $125 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ was divided into five parts of equal area - four squares and one L-shaped figure as shown in the picture. Find the length of the shortest side of the L-shaped figure.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large square containing a 2-by-2 block of four congruent small squares pushed against the top and right sides, leaving an L-shaped strip along the left and bottom. From the text, the total area is 125 cm^2 and the five parts have equal area, so each part has area 25 cm^2. Therefore each of the four square parts has side length 5 cm. The large square has side length sqrt(125)=5\sqrt{5}. The image shows the L-shape's shortest side is exactly the leftover margin after two small-square side lengths fit across the large square, so compute 5\sqrt{5}-2\cdot 5=5(\sqrt{5}-2).

method.method_draft: Read the picture as an outer square and an inner square block made from the four small squares; this inner block touches the top and right sides, so the remaining L-shaped border has uniform thickness t, which is the shortest side requested. From the text, the five regions are equal in area and the total area is 125 cm^2, so the L-shaped region has area 25 cm^2. Thus the area of the inner square block is 125-25=100 cm^2, giving inner block side length 10 cm. The outer square side is sqrt(125)=5\sqrt{5}. Since the L thickness is the difference between the outer square side and the inner block side, t=5\sqrt{5}-10=5(\sqrt{5}-2).
